texts.preamble: Shaik Karimulla, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 13 December, 2019 1 Hon'Ble Sri Justice D.V.S.S. Somayajulu Criminal Petition No.7028 of 2019 Order:
texts.facts: This Criminal Petition is filed to quash all further proceedings in C.C.No.231 of 2018, on the file of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Parchur. F.I.R.No.18 of 2018 of Parchur Police Station has been registered against the accused for the offences under section 273 and 420 IPC. The complaint is that the police have raided the tea stall of the accused and found that the accused has been selling noxious tea powder and cheating the public. Therefore the complaint was lodged and a case was registered for the offencesunder sections 273 and 420 IPC. In the charge sheet ultimately filed, apart from 272 and 420 IPC,Section 59 of the Food Safety Standards Act (in short "FSS Act"), was also included.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner-Accused No.1 essentially questions the FIR on the following three grounds: a) That the 2nd respondent-Sub-Inspector of Police is not competent to register the FIR for the offence under Section 59 of the FSS Act, 2016 or to investigate the same and to lay the charge sheet; b) The offence under Section 273 IPC is non-cognizable and therefore the order of the Magistrate is necessary to conduct investigation; and c) The complainant and the investigating officer is the 2nd respondent only. He also filed the charge sheet. Learned counsel relied upon a judgment of the Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court reported in M/s Pepsico India Holdings (Pvt) Ltd. & Anr.v State of U.P. & Ors.1 to contend that once the provisions of FSS Act come into play, the registration of crime with respect to "food" stuffs can only be done under the FSS Act, 2006. Learned counsel for the petitioner argues that the FSS Act, 2006 is a special enactment created specially by the Parliament and that it eclipses the other provisions of the Indian Penal Code and other special sections. The next submission is that Section 273of IPC is of non-cognizable offence and therefore the order of the jurisdictional Magistrate is necessary. Not but not the least, he says that the same officer is the complainant and the investigating officer. Shaik Karimulla, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 13 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193160922/ 1 Learned Public Prosecutor on the other hand stated that many of the issues that were raised by the learned counsel are matters which need to be decided during the course of the trial and that at this stage quashing the proceedings is not called for. He submits that the proceedings under the IPC and the FSS Act can be taken simultaneously. Therefore, he states that no prejudice is caused if the prosecution is continued.
